Bilevel optimization · SETTING 369

Strongly convex reduced objectives: primitive gradients and objective gaps.

BL_SPEC_sc_gap_primitive

Solve the bilevel problem $\min_x\Phi(x)$, where $\Phi(x)=f(x,y^*(x))$ and $y^*(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_y g(x,y)$ is the unique global lower-level solution. The upper- and lower-level variables are $x\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x}$ and $y\in\mathbb{R}^{d_y}$. Seek approximate stationarity of the reduced objective under the declared criterion and guarantee; assumptions on $f$, $g$, and $\Phi$ are specified separately.

01

Setting specification

Task

Solve the bilevel problem $\min_x\Phi(x)$, where $\Phi(x)=f(x,y^*(x))$ and $y^*(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_y g(x,y)$ is the unique global lower-level solution. The upper- and lower-level variables are $x\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x}$ and $y\in\mathbb{R}^{d_y}$. Return an outer point whose reduced objective value is within $\varepsilon$ of its global minimum on each admissible instance. The admissible model states the assumptions on $f$, $g$, and $\Phi$.

Admissible model

The function $g(x,\cdot)$ is $\mu_y$-strongly convex on all of $\mathbb{R}^{d_y}$, uniformly for $x$. The quantities $\nabla f,\nabla g$ are jointly $L_f,L_g$-Lipschitz, and $g_{xy},g_{yy}$ are respectively $\rho_{xy},\rho_{yy}$-Lipschitz, in Euclidean induced operator norms.

The condition $\|\nabla_y f(x,y)\|\le B_f$ holds everywhere. The public initial point satisfies $\|y_0-y^*(x_0)\|\le R_y$, and there exists $x^*\in\arg\min\Phi$ satisfying $\|x_0-x^*\|\le R_x$. Joint convexity of the primitive $f$ is not assumed.

The reduced objective $\Phi$ is $\mu_x$-strongly convex, with $\mu_x>0$.

Oracle interface

All dimensions, model budgets, and initial points are public. At any $(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_y}$, the algorithm selects $h\in\{f,g\}$ and receives exact full gradient $\nabla h(x,y)$. One call returns only the selected function's gradient. The functions and lower-level optimum remain hidden.

No direct reduced-gradient, lower-level optimum, or inverse-Hessian interface is supplied. Arithmetic based on public data is free.

Queries and responses 1 operations

01 · Declared operation

The interface maps (h,x,y) to exact ∇h(x,y), choosing one h ∈ {f,g} per call.

Output

Return $\widehat{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x}$, which may be an unqueried point or any admissible postprocessing of the transcript. An inner optimizer or certificate is not required.

Loss or accuracy criterion

The base error is $\Phi(\widehat{x})-\Phi^*$, where $\Phi^*=\min_x\Phi(x)$.

Resource accounting

Each primitive gradient call costs one unit; $N=N_{\nabla f}+N_{\nabla g}$. The fixed worst-case budget includes every actual call used in initialization and inner computations.

Algorithm views and success guarantees

Algorithms are deterministic and adaptive. Queries, stopping, and postprocessing may be arbitrary measurable functions of the transcript. The output may be unqueried, a deterministic selection of a past point, or an admissible average. No linear-span or zero-respecting restriction is imposed. Queries are sequential; each actual response in a parallel batch is charged separately. Arithmetic, linear algebra, and storage using received data are uncharged. Internal operations, memory, and communication are not tracked by this quantity.

There exists an algorithm determined by the public inputs such that $\Phi(\widehat{x})-\Phi^*\le\varepsilon$ holds on every admissible instance. The guarantee is deterministic and instancewise.

AccBiO-BG, simulating derivative–vector products by finite differences of exact gradients.

Lower Bounds and Accelerated Algorithms for Bilevel Optimization ↗
Conditions
Tilde notation permits logarithmic factors in $1/\varepsilon$, with all structural budgets fixed. Every original gradient needed by a finite difference is charged separately.
Dimension conditions
The upper bound holds for every finite-dimensional instance in the declared model. Any dimension or fixed-budget dependence not displayed explicitly follows the accompanying evidence qualification.
Algorithm scope
deterministic adaptive algorithm
Correspondence, constants and qualifications
Constants
Unshown regularity, initialization, and noise budgets are fixed. Their joint parameter dependence is not certified as closed.
Derivation
Run the source algorithm at tolerance $\varepsilon/4$ for a fixed finite $K,N,M$ determined by public budgets. Bound finite-step error propagation recursively using public smoothness, distance, and gradient bounds, and allocate derivative-action errors so that the terminal-point perturbation is at most $\sqrt{\varepsilon/(8L_\Phi)}$. Convexity and $L_\Phi$-smoothness give $\|\nabla\Phi(z)\|\le\sqrt{2L_\Phi(\Phi(z)-\Phi^*)}$, so the perturbed objective gap remains at most $\varepsilon$. Use the corresponding block of $[\nabla g(x,y+hv)-\nabla g(x,y)]/h$ for each action, with bias at most $\rho|h|\|v\|^2/2$, choosing sufficiently small nonzero $h$ according to the current $\|v\|$. In the exact-real model without bit costs, smaller steps do not increase the number of primitive queries.
Gap or comparison
An upper bound is available at fixed structural budgets. No lower bound for arbitrary deterministic algorithms under this same specification is currently registered. The Ji–Liang lower bound applies only to the algorithm class in their Definition 2 and therefore does not certify unrestricted optimality.
